comparison: Perfect agreement on GNAI protein localization (C3-C4, C61-C73). Both evaluations find the immunolabeling experiments rigorous and convincing, with OpenEval highlighting the systematic approach across mutants and peer reviewers praising the thoroughness and detailed quantifications.

Perfect agreement on GNAI2 compensation for GNAI3 (C5, C74-C92). Both evaluations support the temporal progression from complete to partial to minimal compensation. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, and OpenEval provides detailed analysis of the quantitative correlations.

Perfect agreement on auditory function results (C55-C60). Both evaluations find the ABR data convincing and note that functional defects mirror morphological findings, with GNAI3 uniquely required for auditory function.

Strong agreement on early GNAI functions in symmetry breaking and bare zone formation (C8, C10, C97-C123). Both evaluations support that Gnai2;Gnai3 double mutants recapitulate pertussis toxin phenotypes. Peer reviewers note that revisions clarified phenotypic differences between genetic and toxin models.

Strong agreement on hair bundle orientation defects (C9, C11, C44-C48, C126-C143). Both evaluations affirm that orientation requires both GNAI2 and GNAI3. OpenEval emphasizes the delayed inversion phenotype and timing effects, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive quantification across developmental stages.

Agreement on GNAI3 as primary protein for hair bundle morphogenesis (C6-C7, C39-C54, C147-C148). Both evaluations support the allelic series and conclude GNAI3 is uniquely required. OpenEval notes the n=1 limitation for double mutants, while peer reviewers emphasize GNAI3's largest effect on development.

Agreement on validation of DIO-ptxA model (C93-C96). Both evaluations find the comparison between DIO-ptxA and LSL-myc:ptxA models convincing. OpenEval details the technical validation, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive collection of mouse models.

Agreement on distinct GNAI roles and mechanistic model (C141-C142, C144-C159 overlap with C145, C149-C159, C161-C164). Both evaluations support the synthesis of findings into a coherent model. Peer reviewers call this the 'authoritative last word' and 'definitive study,' while OpenEval finds the dosage hypothesis and differential role assignments well-supported.

Agreement on reconciliation with previous work (C161-C164). Both evaluations support that the current model explains differences with Beer-Hammer study through mechanistic differences in Cre recombination requirements. Peer reviewers affirm this builds appropriately on earlier reports.

Agreement on background and established knowledge (C14-C38). Both evaluations accept the literature review and contextualization as appropriate. OpenEval notes this sets up key questions, while peer reviewers affirm the study builds on earlier reports without questioning the background.

Agreement on synthesis of distinct GNAI mechanisms (C170-C178). Both evaluations support the distinction between GPR156-GNAI signaling for orientation and GPSM2-GNAI for morphogenesis. This is part of the comprehensive conclusions that peer reviewers find definitive.
Agreement on phylogenetic context (C12-C13). Both evaluations accept the sequence comparison data as appropriate background. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on general statements (C1-C2). Both evaluations support these foundational claims. OpenEval notes they are validated by extensive data, while peer reviewers implicitly accept them as part of the overall study framework.

Agreement on human genetics context (C179-C181). Both evaluations accept the explanation for why GNAI/O proteins haven't been identified as deafness genes. This contextualization is part of the background that peer reviewers do not question.

Agreement on speculative discussion points (C165-C169). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are appropriate discussion points without new supporting data. Peer reviewers do not raise concerns about these speculative elements, implicitly accepting them as reasonable discussion.

Agreement on established knowledge and gaps (C146, C152, C160). Both evaluations accept these claims as appropriate synthesis of known information and identification of future directions. Part of the comprehensive framework that peer reviewers find definitive.
